question: Should OpenClaw intentionally support untrusted external members as an isolation boundary within one gateway, and if so, is this Teams identity, authorization, persistence, and plugin contract the approved v1 architecture?
rationale: Current security policy does not promise adversarial multi-tenancy on one gateway, while this PR creates that promise across authentication, WebSockets, device pairing, persistence, plugins, agents, and the browser; implementation review cannot choose that trust model.

options.title: Approve and stage the boundary
options.body: Approve a written threat model and stable plugin contract, then split and prove the identity, authorization, Workspaces, and portal layers before landing.

options.title: Narrow to trusted collaboration
options.body: Remove the adversarial member boundary and retain only sharing behavior that operates within the existing trusted-operator model.

options.title: Decline core multi-tenancy
options.body: Keep OpenClaw single-operator and route team access through separately isolated gateways or an external owner-controlled service.

recommendation.title: Approve and stage the boundary
recommendation.body: Approve a written threat model and stable plugin contract, then split and prove the identity, authorization, Workspaces, and portal layers before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the Workspaces foundation and is the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether its core trust and plugin boundaries should expand.
